E_mutationTimingEvidence.harness: chapter/qa-mcq-link-producer-p33.html — wrapped Element.prototype.appendChild/insertBefore/replaceChild in the iframe (in-memory only, each wrapper calls through unchanged) plus a MutationObserver on documentElement, installed by a 10ms poll as soon as contentDocument existed
E_mutationTimingEvidence.interpretation: zero captures with 30 links present means the links were NOT inserted as a subtree via appendChild/insertBefore/replaceChild after instrumentation. Two live explanations remain, and this phase cannot choose between them: (1) the links already existed before the wrappers were installed — chapter-app renders synchronously on parse, so a 10ms poll can lose the race; (2) the nodes are materialised by a mechanism the wrappers do not intercept, most plausibly an innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML assignment or a DocumentFragment moved by a method not wrapped.
E_mutationTimingEvidence.confidence: the negative result is reliable; its cause is not determined

F_whyLinkExcludeBypassed: UNKNOWN. What IS proven: the DOM ancestry is correct (closest(LINK_EXCLUDE) resolves to BUTTON.mcq-option), wrapWordsIn itself contains no exclusion test (the guard lives in linkifyDe), and at least four call sites invoke the word-wrappers directly — two of them (:3008, :3830) with no exclusion test at all and on detached nodes.
G_oneProducerForAll14: CONSISTENT BUT UNPROVEN. All 14 share one class signature (bare de-link + role) and one region (button.mcq-option inside .mcq-options), which points to a single producer. Not demonstrated.
H_affectsNonMcqContent: YES for the unguarded call sites in principle: :3008 and :3830 wrap detached sentence units with no exclusion test, and :64 re-sweeps gated containers with no exclusion test. Whether any of these currently produces links inside another excluded region was NOT measured. In b2-15 the breach is mcq-only: .quiz-stage 0, .builder-token/.builder-slot 0, .reading-passage 0.
I_smallestLikelyFixShape: RECOMMENDATION ONLY, and deliberately not chosen: move the exclusion test INTO wrapWordsIn/gatedWrapWordsIn (a single early return per function) instead of relying on every caller to remember it. That makes the guard structural and would neutralise all four direct call sites at once. It must not be applied until the producing call site is identified, because a guard inside the wrapper changes behaviour for :3008/:3830 sentence units too.
J_expectedImpact: ESTIMATE ONLY: −14 HCM, −11 RCB if mcq option text stops being linkified. Unchanged from Phase 31/32 since the target set has not moved.

correctionsToEarlierPhases: Phase 32 inferred from "no data-linked marker" that neither linkifier processed these hosts. That inference is now WEAKENED: the lexicon-onload re-sweep at :73 calls wrapWordsIn directly WITHOUT setting dataset.linked, so a marker-less host is not proof that linkifyDe was bypassed. The producer question is genuinely open, not narrowed to a "third subsystem".
